# FEVER IN AN ASPLENIC PATIENT

Patients with impaired splenic function are at risk for severe and overwhelming

infection with encapsulated bacteria. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most

common cause of fulminant sepsis in patients with impaired splenic function,

followed by Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis. Infection with

Capnocytophaga species is possible in asplenic patients with anteceding

scratches and animal bites, especially dog bites. Babesiosis is also more likely

in asplenic patients exposed to tick bites.

If fever develops in an asplenic patient, immediate administration of an

antimicrobial agent is indicated, because fever can be the initial manifestation

of a fulminant infection and prompt administration of an antimicrobial agent may

prevent the development of clinical sepsis.

Administration of antibiotics should not be delayed for performing diagnostic

studies, including lumbar puncture.

# Streptococcus pneumoniae meningitis suspected

[Bacterial meningitis with S. pneumoniae](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-s-pneumoniae)

# Anteceding animal bite or scratch

Consult Infectious Diseases

For tick bites consider treatment for Babesia species

[Babesia Species](orzid2-gmenu-babesia-spp)

Other animal bites or scratches

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)
